title: A refused page re-lay leaves the window drawing the page band over no page
body:
## Summary
When Rust refuses `layout_select("page")`, `depth/shape.ts` logs it and the stage still draws the page shape: a band over a scene-shaped window with nothing in it.

## Description
`startShapeSync` (apps/desktop/src/depth/shape.ts:23-27) sets `last = shape` before the send and only `console.error`s a rejection, so the depth stays at `apps/<item>/page` while Rust kept the scene layout. `Stage` (apps/desktop/src/stage/Stage.tsx, `shape === "page"`) then draws only the bar and band and no water, scenes or dock, because ADR 0088 assumes Rust has clipped the document to the band. Nothing tells the person, and the only way out is Rise or Escape. Fixed looks like: on a refusal for the shape the depth is still in, the depth returns to the place it came from (as `console/follow.ts` followLayout already does for a layout Rust changed on its own) and `last` is cleared, so a retry is possible. State-coverage: the FAIL state renders like success.

## Flow
- open a page from the Apps depth while the shell refuses the re-lay (no page webview, a window mid-teardown)
- shape.ts sends `page`, the promise rejects, console.error only
- the stage draws data-shape=page: the 76 px band and an empty window below it
- proposal: in the catch, if shapeOf(useDepth.getState().path) is still the refused shape, rise to parentOf and reset `last`

## Expected impact
A person whose page could not be shown lands back on the app's item instead of an empty window. Could break: a transient refusal followed by Rust's own `layout-changed` might now double-move; follow.ts's guard (null when the depth agrees) should absorb it.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a refused re-lay returns the depth to a drawable place
Before: shape.test.ts 'survives a re-lay that is refused' only asserts console.error; the depth stays at the page path (walked)
After: not measured
Method: simulation - three walked cases (refusal at start, on dive to page, on rise); the gate rung needs the shape.test case and the decision of rise-vs-notice
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: a shape.test.ts case: send rejects for 'page' after go(apps/a/page); assert the store path returns to apps/a and a later page dive sends again

title: An interrupted move restarts the half-arrived layer's leave at full opacity
body:
## Summary
`stage/layers.ts` promises that a layer interrupted while arriving "starts leaving from wherever it got to", but the CSS swaps its animation-name, which restarts the leave keyframes from opacity 1 and no transform.

## Description
On a move during a move, `reduceLayers` (apps/desktop/src/stage/layers.ts:54-55) turns the arriving layer's phase from `enter-*` to `leave-*`. In apps/desktop/src/stage/stage.css:332-364 each phase is a different `animation-name`, and a new animation starts at its `from` keyframe: `leave-down` from `opacity: 1; transform: none`. A dive interrupted 100 ms in (layer at roughly opacity 0.4, scale 0.93) snaps to full opacity and full size for one frame, then fades. The header comment states the opposite, so this is also a stale claim (copy-auditor). Registry: motion/engine-selection ('deciding whether a gesture can be interrupted mid-flight'): keyframe animations are not interruptible from their current value; a transition on opacity/transform, or reading the current computed value into the leave's from, is.

## Flow
- dive (Surface to Apps), and within ~150 ms press Escape or click another root
- the arriving Apps layer becomes leave-up: animation-name changes, keyframes restart
- observed (predicted): the half-faded layer flashes to opacity 1, then fades out
- proposal: drive enter/leave by transitions on opacity and transform (phase sets the target), so an interruption reverses from the current value; keep the 360 ms clock and Calm

## Expected impact
Rapid navigators stop seeing a flash on interrupted moves; perf:stage already drives an interrupted dive. Could break: animationend-based settling would become transitionend-based, and the SAFETY flush stays the backstop.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - an interrupted layer never brightens on its way out
Before: not measured; CSS semantics say the leave restarts at opacity 1 (stage.css:345-347)
After: not measured
Method: simulation - needs per-frame opacity sampling in a browser (perf-gate drive); jsdom has no animations
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: extend scripts/perf-stage.drive.mjs's interrupted dive to sample getComputedStyle(layer).opacity each frame for the interrupted layer and assert it never increases after the interrupt

title: The Mind and Voice level lists are hand-kept beside the depth grammar's items
body:
## Summary
`scenes/mind/view.tsx` INSTRUMENTS and the Voice scene's studio/settings checks repeat the grammar's fixed items (`depth/model.ts` GRAMMAR) with no test between them.

## Description
GRAMMAR (apps/desktop/src/depth/model.ts:53-62) fixes `voice: [studio, settings]` and `mind: [engine, brain, look, data, mic]` and is private. The Mind scene keeps its own `INSTRUMENTS` (apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/view.tsx:70) and the Voice view tests `path.item !== "studio" && path.item !== "settings"` (apps/desktop/src/scenes/voice/view.tsx:63). A level added to the scene and not the grammar renders a button whose `go` the reducer silently ignores (`moveTo` returns the state for an invalid path); one added to the grammar and not the scene is a link that lands on a level the scene cannot draw. The registry already records the module-design deviation for `stage/preview.tsx` re-encoding GRAMMAR (not re-proposed); this is the product pair, outside this context's paths. Fix: export a read of a root's fixed items from model.ts and pin each scene's list to it.

## Flow
- add 'keys' to INSTRUMENTS and its art; leave GRAMMAR alone
- click the new Mind button: go({root:'mind', item:'keys'}) is ignored by reduce, nothing happens, no error
- proposal: model.ts exports itemsOf(root); mind/view.test and voice/view.test assert equality

## Expected impact
A future Mind or Voice level cannot ship half-wired. Could break: nothing at runtime; a test-only pin plus one exported read.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one list for a root's levels, or a test that fails when two drift
Before: 0 tests compare INSTRUMENTS or the Voice items with GRAMMAR (grep)
After: not built
Method: probe - git grep over apps/desktop/src for the lists; the build sits in scenes/mind and scenes/voice, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: export itemsOf(root) from depth/model.ts; a mind/view.test case INSTRUMENTS == itemsOf('mind') and a voice/view.test case for ['studio','settings'], each seeded red by adding a level on one side

title: The dock's Athena button does not say it goes to the surface
body:
## Summary
The dock's Athena button and the bar's brand both call onSurface, but only the brand's name says so; the dock's is read as "Athena, <her state>, N waiting".

## Description
apps/desktop/src/stage/Stage.tsx:154: the brand button carries `aria-label="Athena, back to the surface"`; the dock's `stage__dock-athena` button takes its name from its content (Athena, `presence.text`, the waiting count) and nothing says what pressing it does. Two controls for one action, named two ways (copy-auditor: two names for one concept). Registry: accessibility/name-and-description-wiring - the name should carry the action; her state belongs in the description. Fix: name it like the brand and move the presence to aria-describedby (or a visually hidden 'back to the surface' in the name), keeping the visible text unchanged.

## Flow
- dive to any depth with a screen reader on; Tab to the dock
- heard: 'Athena Resting button' (no destination)
- the brand two Tab stops up is heard as 'Athena, back to the surface'

## Expected impact
Screen-reader users learn from the control itself that it returns to the surface. Could break: a test or e2e that finds the dock button by its text content.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the dock button's accessible name names its action
Before: name = content text 'Athena' + presence text + waiting (read from the markup)
After: not built
Method: probe - read the rendered markup in Stage.test.tsx; wording of the name/description split is a copy call the round did not make
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: apps/desktop/src/stage/Stage.tsx:154
instrument: a Stage.test.tsx case asserting the dock button's aria-label (or labelled-by text) contains 'surface' and its description carries presence.text; seeded red on the current markup

title: A held Escape walks all the way to the surface
body:
## Summary
`escapeRises` ignores key repeat, so holding Escape a moment past the OS repeat delay rises one level per repeat, from depth 3 to the surface.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/stage/Stage.tsx `escapeRises` (apps/desktop/src/stage/Stage.tsx:70) checks key, defaultPrevented and typing, not `e.repeat`; the window keydown listener calls onRise for every repeat. ADR 0087 says Escape 'rises a level'. Whether a held Escape should keep rising (a fast way home) or rise once per press is a product call, not a defect the code can settle: the surface has its own one-click way (the brand, the dock).

## Flow
- be at apps/<item>/tool/<name> (depth 3); press and hold Escape ~0.6 s
- OS autorepeat fires keydown with repeat=true; each one rises
- observed: lands on the surface, three moves played back to back

## Expected impact
If decided 'once per press': rapid accidental holds stop losing the person's depth. Could break: anyone using the hold as a shortcut home.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one press, one level
Before: rises per repeat event (read from escapeRises; no repeat check)
After: not built
Method: probe - read the pure rule and the listener; the benefit is a direction call
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: apps/desktop/src/stage/Stage.tsx:70 export function escapeRises(e: { key: string; defaultPrevented: boolean; targetIsTyping: boolean }) { return e.key === "Escape" && !e.defaultPrevented && !e.targetIsTyping; }
